claims.text: An exit plan is best written when the vendor is chosen, while the team knows every place the vendor is used and can still ask for contract terms the plan needs, such as data export in a stated format.

Named triggers make leaving a decision against criteria written in calm conditions; untried steps are a guess, as an untested backup is; after a trigger a new evaluation picks the next vendor; if work begun with the old vendor can only finish there, an overlap period follows.
claims.source_hint: Outline items 4-5; misconceptions 2-3; devops.l3.restore-testing summary line 1

claims.text: ADR 0010's triggers: Gateway A misses its availability promise three months out of six in a row; it announces the end of the API version in use with no replacement giving the three outcomes; renewal price rises more than the contract allows.

ADR 0010's steps: (1) new evaluation with the same criteria; (2) a new client returning the same three outcomes as GatewayRefundClient, with tests; refund saga, RefundSender and other services unchanged; (5) after the overlap, remove the old client and Gateway A's configuration.

RefundOutcome in DonHang.Payments/GatewayRefundClient.cs has three values: Refunded, Refused, TryAgainLater; the class is the anti-corruption layer; RefundSender is the background job that calls the gateway for each due refund.
claims.source_hint: DonHang.Payments/GatewayRefundClient.cs @ stage-3 lines 9-14, 39-43; DonHang.Payments/RefundSender.cs @ stage-3 class comment

claims.text: Step 3: refund history exported from Gateway A as CSV under the data export term and kept with the backups so accounting can still reconcile after the contract ends.

Step 4: both gateways run for a period; a payment taken by Gateway A can only be refunded through Gateway A, so each refund row must know which gateway took its payment, until the last Gateway A payment's 180-day refund window ends.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0010-cong-thanh-toan-ben-ngoai.md @ stage-3 lines 59-62; payment-gateway-evaluation.md T5 (Gateway A 180 days)

claims.text: ADR 0010 estimates 10-20 person-days for steps 2 to 4, not counting the evaluation.

Testable part: export refund history from the test env (lab: GET /v1/refunds on fake-gateway, the lab's stand-in for Gateway A), load into a table made for the check, compare row count and amounts with the refund rows of payments (donhang_payments) marked refunded; the table also holds charge rows.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0010 @ stage-3 lines 67-73; fake-gateway/Program.cs @ stage-3 GET /v1/refunds comment; DonHang.Payments/PaymentsDbContext.cs (kind charge/refund); Payment.cs (pending/refunded/failed)

claims.text: ADR 0009's exit plan is short because sign-in uses OpenID Connect, which keeps most sign-in code provider-neutral. Triggers: Keycloak stops security fixes for the line in use, or operating work exceeds 20 days a year two years running.

ADR 0009: export users from Keycloak; if the new provider cannot take the hashed passwords, customers reset theirs at first sign-in; API changes are the Program.cs line reading the role claim (the token payload field listing the user's roles) and the provider's address.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0009 @ stage-3 lines 75-78; DonHang.Api/Program.cs @ stage-3 line 73 (RoleClaimType)

claims.text: ADR 0010 chooses Gateway A after ruling Gateway B out on a knock-out criterion (T1) and contains its exit plan in the same record.
Once the contract is signed, a missing export term is much harder to get, at best at the next renewal; the trigger (an API or contract end date) sets the day the move must be done.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 2; misconception 2; docs/team/payment-gateway-evaluation.md @ stage-3 lines 80-81 (auto-renewal)

claims.text: Try it: Gateway A refunds up to 180 days after payment, so if its last payment is on a Sunday, step 5 can happen at the earliest the day after that window closes; the new gateway never took Gateway A's payments, so the team keeps the history.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/payment-gateway-evaluation.md @ stage-3 line 45; docs/adr/0010 @ stage-3 lines 56-63

claims.text: If a trigger fires and the team chooses a new gateway, that decision would supersede ADR 0010.
ADR 0010 says its exit plan was written as soon as Gateway A was chosen; the decision was made in Sprint 15 and recorded as an ADR in Sprint 16.
